did_you_know.text: The wall had already been almost completely rebuilt, but the city gates had not yet been installed.
Sanballat and Geshem invited Nehemiah to meet them in the plain of Ono, but Nehemiah realized that they intended to harm him.
The invitation to meet was sent to Nehemiah four times, and each time he gave the same reply and refused to leave his work.
The fifth time, Sanballat sent Nehemiah an open letter rather than a sealed one, accusing him of rebellion.
Sanballat claimed that Nehemiah and the Jews were rebuilding the wall in order to rebel against the king, and that Nehemiah intended to become king in Jerusalem.
Nehemiah realized that the threats were meant to weaken the workers, so he asked God to strengthen his hands and help him continue the work.
Shemaiah suggested that Nehemiah hide inside the temple to protect himself from assassination, but Nehemiah refused to enter a place he was not permitted to enter.
Nehemiah realized that the advice he had received was part of a plot intended to make him sin, so that his enemies could discredit him.
The wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, after fifty-two days of work.
Even after the wall was completed, letters continued to be exchanged between the nobles of Judah and Tobiah, and marriage ties strengthened his connections with Jewish families.
